# Two actual deepest bases need not have a paying common endpoint core

This is an exact n=d=1 counterexample to an auxiliary geometric implication. There are four positive actual interval fibers, exactly two inner deepest points of opposite parity, and regular critical circuits. Nevertheless no regular critical circuit at the first source has an interior common cap intersection in the left endpoint fiber. This does NOT refute a potential-efficiency bound: in this dimension the two circuit weights themselves supply Gamma_1=1/2.

## 1. Actual convex body and complete fibers

At integer bases 0,1,2,3 prescribe

    K0=[47/50,26/25],
    K1=[-11/10,1],
    K2=[-23/25,23/25],
    K3=[-9/100,9/100].                                 (1)

Their lower endpoint increments are -51/25,9/50,83/100, a nondecreasing sequence. Their upper endpoint increments are -1/25,-2/25,-83/100, a nonincreasing sequence. The piecewise-affine lower and upper roofs therefore define a compact convex body in R^2 with nonempty interior and these exact integer fibers. Its projection [0,3] has no other integer points. Its mixed one-dimensional mass is

    M=1/10+21/10+46/25+9/50=211/50.                    (2)

Every fiber is strictly lighter than M/2=211/100, including the largest one of length21/10=210/100. This also gives every strict proper-closed-minor count quota: a singleton has mass less than M/2, whereas every closed set of at least two bases contains consecutive integers and has both parities, so its properness gives mass less than M. The smallest normalized quota gap is at least1/422.

## 2. Four actual critical caps and their covering property

At Y1=(1,0) take

    H+={x-(z-1)>=0},
    H-={-x-(93/100)(z-1)>=0}.                           (3)

The first captures K0 strictly and the part [0,1] of K1, and strictly misses K2,K3. Its mass is 1/10+1=11/10. The second strictly misses all fibers except K1 and captures [-11/10,0] there. Its mass is also 11/10.

At Y2=(2,0) take

    J+={x+2(z-2)>=0},
    J-={-x+2(z-2)>=0}.                                  (4)

Both strictly miss K0,K1, capture a half of K2 of length23/25, and capture all of K3 strictly. Their masses are23/25+9/50=11/10.

Every displayed cut is proper only in its own source interval and strictly full or empty elsewhere. Thus the full cap-mass function is differentiable in all hyperplane parameters. The only section point is the source, with coarea one. Continuous normals are +1,-1, so each group is a regular positive circuit with normalized response weights 1/2,1/2. Both integer tilts at Y1 are negative; both at Y2 are positive.

The two margins in (3) sum to -(193/100)(z-1), so their closed union covers the entire continuous line over every z<=1. The margins in (4) sum to 4(z-2), so their union covers every line over z>=2. Consequently the four caps cover the whole actual mixed set and show that its maximum raw depth is at most

    Q=11/10.                                           (5)

## 3. Exact lower bound for all ambient halfspaces

At either Yp=(p,0), every nonvertical through-point cap can be written as x>=t(z-p), or as its closed reverse. Define its captured mass

    F_p(t)=sum_(z=0)^3 clamp(u_z-t(z-p),0,u_z-l_z),       (6)

where [l_z,u_z]=Kz and clamp(s,0,w)=max(0,min(s,w)). Its reverse has mass M-F_p(t), since the boundary meets every fiber in at most a point of zero length.

The function (6) is continuous and piecewise affine. Its only possible slope breakpoints are t=l_z/(z-p) and t=u_z/(z-p), with z!=p. It is constant beyond the two outermost breakpoints. Thus its minimum and maximum are determined EXACTLY by the following finite tables; no numerical sampling or restriction on normal orientation is used.

For p=1:

| t | F_1(t) |
|---|---:|
| -infinity through -26/25 | 151/50 |
| -47/50 | 78/25 |
| -23/25 | 78/25 |
| -9/200 | 449/200 |
| 9/200 | 79/40 |
| 23/25 through +infinity | 11/10 |

The entries -26/25,-47/50 come from K0, -23/25,23/25 from K2, and -9/200,9/200 from K3. Between consecutive listed knots F is affine. Its minimum is11/10 and maximum is78/25=M-11/10.

For p=2:

| t | F_2(t) |
|---|---:|
| -infinity through -1 | 11/10 |
| -13/25 | 79/50 |
| -47/100 | 173/100 |
| -9/100 | 211/100 |
| 9/100 | 211/100 |
| 11/10 through +infinity | 78/25 |

The entries -1,11/10 come from K1, -13/25,-47/100 from K0, and -9/100,9/100 from K3. Again both orientations have minimum captured mass11/10.

Pure-integer through-point halfspaces must also be retained. At p=1 their two masses are11/5 and103/25, and at p=2 their masses are101/25 and101/50. Each exceeds11/10, including the entire source fiber on the closed boundary. Any containing halfspace contains its parallel through-point halfspace. Therefore BOTH Y1,Y2 have raw depth at least Q for every closed ambient halfspace.

Together with (5) this proves exact global depth

    max depth_S=Q/M=55/211.                            (7)

The two points are the only globally deepest points. At either endpoint an exposing finite base tilt isolates its ordinary interval depth, at most half its length (1/20 or9/100), below Q. At an inner point other than its displayed mark, one of that source's two critical caps contains the point strictly. Raising that cap threshold a sufficiently small positive amount retains the point and removes positive length from its proper own interval. It then has mass below Q. This proves uniqueness within each inner fiber without a differentiability assumption at the competing point.

## 4. Failure of the endpoint core, including every regular circuit choice

At base zero the two traces in (3) are

    (H+)_0={x>=-1},
    (H-)_0={x<=93/100}.

Their common intersection is[-1,93/100], whereas K0 starts at47/50=94/100. The common core therefore misses even the CLOSED endpoint body, by a gap1/100. The affine extrapolation of the two deepest marks is x=0, also outside K0.

In fact selecting a different regular circuit at Y1 cannot produce an interior endpoint core. The complete table in Section 3 gives ALL critical through-Y1 cuts:

* In the orientation x>=t(z-1), criticality holds exactly for t>=23/25.
* In the reverse orientation x<=t(z-1), criticality holds exactly for -47/50<=t<=-23/25.

Every positive circuit in one continuous dimension must use both orientations. Every negative-orientation critical cap has at base zero the upper trace x<=-t<=47/50, so its intersection with int K0 is empty. At t=-47/50 it meets only the lower endpoint, and at t=-23/25 it also has a supporting trace on K2. These endpoint cases are nonregular in d=1 because a supporting point has positive H_0 coarea; interior parameters are regular and strictly miss K0. Positive-orientation critical caps are regular for t>23/25 and contain all of K0.

Thus no finite regular critical circuit at Y1 has

    int K0 intersect intersection_j (H_j)_0 != empty.   (8)

There are no critical pure-integer caps by Section 3. Moreover all critical caps at Y1 miss K3 strictly, so the opposite exposed endpoint does not provide an alternative common core.

## 5. Exact scope of the obstruction

This family retains actual convexity, complete consecutive integer sampling, positive strictly nonheavy fibers, all strict proper-closed-minor count quotas, two genuine inner deepest bases occupying both parities, and regular critical menus. It refutes the inference from those premises to a nonempty exposed endpoint core, even after favorable regular-circuit selection. It does not refute the more general selected convex-potential efficiency assertion.

For the pair (3), the profile at K0 is identically 1/2: H+ contains it and H- misses it. Any nonzero endpoint-localized potential therefore has efficiency exactly Gamma_1=1/2. The failure is specifically in requiring all row traces to contain one common endpoint mark. A weighted profile can pay without this common-point property.

The normalized depth55/211 is above the one-integer, one-continuous target1/4, by9/844. A bad-depth hypothesis is not satisfied. No higher-dimensional product extension is asserted: adding continuous coordinates would require a new all-oblique lower bound.

The affine-on-each-complete-cell argument is what certifies all slopes, not the extra sample checks inside those cells.
